the molecular mechanism of NMD, a process that is essential for cellular viability and that has been linked to a variety of genetic diseases in humans.
the identification of a putative orthologue of the human NMD proteins Smg5 and Smg7 in yeast and the characterization of its function in NMD and its interaction with other NMD proteins.

Ebs1 is a putative yeast ortholog of human NMD factor Smg7.
the NMD pathway is conserved from yeast to humans, but that there are differences in the molecular details of the pathway.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ebs1 protein is an NMD factor in S. cerevisiae that is structurally and functionally similar to human Smg7.
Ebs1 is an ortholog of human SMG7 and that EBS1 and SMG7 are both required for the efficient degradation of nonsense mRNA.
Ebs1 is a Smg7 ortholog in S. cerevisiae and that it functions in NMD by interacting with Upf1 and by promoting the recruitment of Upf proteins to P-bodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NMD is a more conserved process than previously thought.
the Smg5, 6, 7 proteins are not essential for NMD in either yeast or human cells, and the Smg5/7 proteins may be involved in a backup pathway for NMD.
NMD is a conserved process, which has been maintained in the course of evolution, despite its complexity and involvement of multiple proteins.
